question: When counselling a mother on complementary feeding at 6 months, the doctor should advise that breastfeeding can be stopped once the infant is established on solid foods, typically by 8-9 months of age.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Breastfeeding should NOT be stopped when complementary foods are started. The WHO/IAP recommendation is to continue breastfeeding for 2 years or beyond while complementary foods are introduced from 6 months. Breast milk remains a nutritionally important food throughout the second year.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Breastfeeding should continue alongside complementary foods for 2 years or beyond, as per WHO/IAP recommendations. Stopping breastfeeding at 8-9 months deprives the infant of immunological protection, continued nutrition, and the developmental benefits of breastfeeding.
